name: Aiyarappar Temple, Thiruvaiyaru
deity: Shiva as Aiyarappar (Panchanadeeswarar), with the goddess Aram Valartha Nayaki (Dharmasamvardhini)
period: Ancient Shaiva shrine on the Kaveri; Chola and later additions; sung in the Tevaram (7th century)
summary: Aiyarappar is the great Shiva temple of Thiruvaiyaru on the Kaveri, the Dakshina Kailasam where Appar beheld a vision of Kailasa, the heart of the Sapta Sthanam festival, and the town of the saint-composer Thyagaraja.

sections.history: Thiruvaiyaru, whose name is read as the town of the five rivers, has been a place of pilgrimage since at least the seventh century, when Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar sang of Aiyarappar in the Tevaram, making this a Paadal Petra Sthalam. The temple is rooted in the Chola country and its patrons, and over the centuries it grew into a large complex of about fifteen acres with five enclosures. Appar is believed to have been granted a vision of Kailasa here, which is why the shrine is called Dakshina Kailasam, the Kailasa of the South. In later times the town found a second renown as the home of the saint-composer Thyagaraja, whose music is remembered on the Kaveri bank nearby.
sections.architecture: The complex is entered beneath a seven-tiered rajagopuram and is enclosed by five courts. Sacred tirthams, among them the Surya, Nandi, Samudra and Devamritha tanks, are associated with the temple, and the Kaveri itself is counted among its waters. Two sanctums stand at the heart of worship, one for Aiyarappar and one for the goddess Aram Valartha Nayaki, also known as Dharmasamvardhini, whose name speaks of virtue nurtured. Long Dravidian corridors, mandapas and carved pillars give the enclosure the unhurried air of a place built for processions.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that Nandi, the sacred bull, was born here to the sage Salankayana and grew up under the temple's shelter; the Sapta Sthanam procession is tied to the tradition of his wedding. It is also told that Appar, striving to reach Kailasa, was bidden to bathe in a sacred tank at Thiruvaiyaru, and rising from the water he beheld Shiva and Parvati and their attendants all around him. In this way the story gives Thiruvaiyaru its place as a Kailasa that pilgrims of the south can reach.
sections.festivals: The Sapta Sthanam festival, usually in April or May, is the great event of the year: the palanquins of seven neighbouring Shiva temples gather in a joyful procession. In the cool season the Thyagaraja Aradhana draws musicians from across the country to the Kaveri bank to sing the saint's compositions in his memory. Maha Shivaratri and the monthly Pradosham are kept as at every Shiva temple. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Come in the cool of the morning, when the courts are quiet and the Kaveri lies close by. Walk through the long enclosures to the sanctum of Aiyarappar, then to the shrine of the goddess, and pause at the tirthams. Many visitors pair the temple with a walk to the Kaveri bank, where the memory of Thyagaraja is strongest and musicians gather in season. Thiruvaiyaru is an unhurried town, and the temple suits those who like to linger.

visit.timings: Typically open in the morning and again from late afternoon into the evening, with a midday break; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected: dhotis or trousers for men, sarees, salwar kameez, or long skirts for women, with shoulders and knees covered. Footwear is left at the entrance stands.
visit.photography: Photography is generally permitted in the outer corridors and courtyards but strictly prohibited inside the inner sanctum, in keeping with Tamil Nadu temple rules. Ask temple staff before photographing rituals or priests.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruvaiyaru lies on the Kaveri, about 13 km from Thanjavur, and is reached by frequent buses and by road from Thanjavur, Kumbakonam and Tiruchirappalli. Thanjavur is the nearest large railhead, and Tiruchirappalli International Airport, around 60 km away, is the nearest airport. The temple stands in the town centre, and autos are easily found.
